questions.text: What is the primary purpose of RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)?
options: To pre-train language models on web-scale data
To compress models for efficient inference
To replace supervised fine-tuning entirely
To align model outputs with human preferences for helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty
questions.explanation: RLHF uses human preference feedback to fine-tune models so their outputs better align with what humans consider helpful, safe, and truthful. It is typically applied after supervised fine-tuning as an alignment step.

questions.text: In the RLHF pipeline, what is the role of the reward model?
options: To generate training data for pre-training
To score model outputs based on learned human preferences, providing a reward signal for RL training
To tokenize the input text before it enters the policy model
To select which layers to freeze during training
questions.explanation: The reward model is trained on human comparison data to predict which outputs humans prefer. During RL training, it assigns scalar reward scores to the policy model's outputs, guiding the optimization process.

questions.text: Which of the following are key components of the PPO algorithm as used in RLHF? Select all that apply
options: A clipped surrogate objective to prevent large policy updates
Contrastive learning between positive and negative examples
A KL divergence penalty to keep the policy close to the reference model
Dropout regularization applied to the reward model
questions.explanation: PPO uses a clipped surrogate objective to ensure stable policy updates, and a KL divergence penalty is typically added in RLHF to prevent the policy model from deviating too far from the initial supervised fine-tuned model, which could lead to reward hacking.

questions.text: How is the reward model typically trained in the RLHF pipeline?
options: Using next-token prediction on a large corpus
Using reinforcement learning with environment rewards
On human comparison data where annotators rank or choose between model outputs
By distilling a larger teacher model
questions.explanation: The reward model is trained on datasets where human annotators compare pairs of model outputs and indicate which one is preferred. The model learns to assign higher scores to preferred outputs using a ranking or Bradley-Terry loss.

questions.text: What is "reward hacking" in the context of RLHF?
options: When the policy model exploits flaws in the reward model to achieve high scores without genuinely improving quality
When the reward model is trained on too much data
When human annotators intentionally provide incorrect labels
When the learning rate is set too high during PPO training
questions.explanation: Reward hacking occurs when the policy model learns to produce outputs that receive high reward scores by exploiting imperfections in the reward model, rather than generating genuinely better content. KL penalties help mitigate this problem.
